goal.task: Add a reset operation to the existing counter.count capability on the hello_world backend
goal.behavior: counter.count gains a reset operation that clears every per-word count; subsequent count calls start over from 1
goal.compatibility: backward compatible -- the existing count operation and its per-word semantics must not change
goal.test_required: the verification harness must exercise reset and prove counts start over after it
goal.integration_required: route it through the existing ARPAPED Bridge (sample/hello_world/backend/runtime/bridge) without modifying the Bridge's architecture

starting_state: last completed cycle's published state at sample/hello_world/backend: counter.count 1.0.0 with operation count verified 23/23 and recorded as episode hello-world-e09e9222d084; catalog has 7 implementation records; verified-green verification-record.json present
reusable_discovery: sample/hello_world/backend/implementation/contracts/counter.count.contract.yaml and its manifest/executor (exactly one contract file per capability, R2)

decisions.reason: Adds a backward-compatible reset operation to the existing counter.count capability; Phase 3 discovery found no registered capability anywhere providing reset/clear semantics to reuse or compose. R1 small-reusability verdict: 'clear accumulated counts' is a generic single-task operation, a natural peer of count within the same capability. Recorded per R2 as a new version peer (1.1.0: operations count + reset) in the one contract file; 1.0.0 stays a recorded, supported peer (backward compatibility), and the single implementation counter.count.default upgrades to 1.1.0.

registry_changes: capability-catalog.jsonl rebuilt via build_catalog: still 7 implementation records; the counter.count.default entry updated to contract_version 1.1.0, implementation version 1.1.0, operations [count, reset] (input_schema now records both operations). assemble_from_catalog registers it into the canonical Registry at requests.py import time.
bridge_integration: Every backend call (the existing six plus hello_counter count x4 and reset x1) resolved through app/requests.py's single request-construction point and the same canonical Bridge app/main.py uses (R6/R8). The frontend greeting_render check still boots web.serve via that same resolve() and exercises the frontend's own Bridge over web.serve's /bridge endpoint. No Bridge component (bridge.py/registry.py/policy.py/selector.py/assembler.py) was modified.

verification.trace_evaluation: All 12 backend capability-operation calls observed full Bridge traces validated -> discovered -> policy_evaluated -> selected -> executed (copied verbatim from responses), including counter.count reset (call 10); the frontend's greeting_render observed the same through its own Bridge. counter.count's six calls observed running counts [1, 2, 1, 0, 1, 1], asserting in-process persistence AND reset semantics (call:7-12:hello_counter:in-process-persistence-and-reset).
verification.failures_and_fixes: No failures this cycle: first harness run after the reset changes passed 26/26. The previous cycle's harness-infrastructure correction (stop calling save_episode; defer to finish_cycle) remains in force.
